subject.title: [Bug]: Subagents can appear completed before the underlying delegated work is actually finished

question: Should child-owned background exec/process sessions block subagent completion, or should they be surfaced as separate active work after the child agent turn completes?
rationale: Both contracts are plausible: blocking avoids false completion, but detached process work is already a separate scoped registry and could intentionally outlive the child agent turn.

options.title: Surface active child processes separately
options.body: Keep subagent completion tied to the child agent-run terminal state, but show child-owned running processes in task/session status and parent handoff so users are not told all delegated work is done.

options.title: Block completion on owned process liveness
options.body: Defer subagent task success until scoped child-owned processes settle, with explicit timeout, cancel, cleanup, and detached-work escape rules.

options.title: Document current semantics
options.body: Treat subagent completion as the child agent turn ending and document that background exec work must be tracked through process/task status.

recommendation.title: Surface active child processes separately
recommendation.body: Keep subagent completion tied to the child agent-run terminal state, but show child-owned running processes in task/session status and parent handoff so users are not told all delegated work is done.

likelyOwner.reason: The highest-confidence history is the merged descendant-gating and announce-delivery work on the same subagent completion surface.
